question: How do the selected native screen-manager update, controller replacement and retirement requests change current-controller storage, and which lifetime and invocation relations remain unresolved?

scope.qualification: Seven complete PE bodies establish the selected local lifecycle ordering. The UI queue topic owns the referenced reader. Actual controller/provider/key, callback retention, completed ownership and key-2/loading-pump invocation remain conditional.

dependencies.use: Accepted manager/child/key construction, separate loading-object lifetime, caller global clear and distinct departure-controller observations.
Accepted key-1/key-2 state-dispatch order and key-2 update identity, without a cancellation or pump-invocation inference.
Only the selected manager construction, retained-vector pop and registry-provider selection relations.
Canonical deferred-reader behavior and exact reused 58-word reader identity.

currentEvidence.method: Serialized foreground read-only radius-zero queries matched the supported image and narrow exact-owner generated operand comments with independent Capstone 5.0.7 decoding. Complete PE extents and big-endian word digests identify the seven lifecycle bodies. The queue topic separately owns the referenced reader; static checks establish no runtime result.
currentEvidence.qualification: Current vptr/target and storage retention, helper/free results, record/controller generation, supported vector ownership and actual invocation remain separate premises.

roles: P is the retained manager argument, normally sampled from U32[0x8314F2E4]. P+4 is its current controller, +8/+0x0C/+0x2C are separate children, +0x10 is its recorded key, +0x18 contains the embedded queued-record container, +0x28 its current count, and +0x30 the retained-controller pointer vector. Bytes +0x40/+0x41 select replacement branches. Distinct reads are not assumed to retain the same object or value across callbacks.
selectedRelations: Cell 0x82131090 identifies key-1 state update +8 as 0x82E7E3E0. Cell 0x82165680 identifies the manager deleting-destructor request as 0x822FDBF0. Manager progress is reached by the selected direct call from the key-1 update.

updateRequest.stateWrapper: 0x82E7E3E0 samples global P at 0x82E7E3F0 and requests 0x82C568C8(P) at 0x82E7E3F4 without a null guard. On normal return it returns one. This key-1 update relation alone does not place that update inside key-2 entry or the separate H+0x78 loading pump.
updateRequest.managerProgress: 0x82C568C8 first samples C=P+4 and, when nonnull, requests C current virtual +8 at 0x82C568F4. It then samples P+0x2C; a nonnull child whose byte +8 is nonzero receives virtual +0 with argument 1 at 0x82C56920, followed by P+0x2C=0 after normal return.
updateRequest.switchAdmission: After those calls, 0x82C5692C freshly samples C=P+4. Null C, a mismatch between C+8 and P+0x10, or nonzero P+0x41 admits the switch. The selected arithmetic at 0x82C56954..0x82C56968 writes the low32 two's-complement absolute-value transform of P+0x10 before requesting 0x82C56638. Input 0x80000000 remains 0x80000000; this is not an all-input nonnegative-key theorem.
updateRequest.tailRequest: After either switch admission or bypass, 0x82C5698C requests current virtual +0x44 of the object freshly loaded from 0x8314F28C with arguments 0 and 1. Its effects and return remain separate.

replacement.acceptedSelection: The accepted producer boundary owns retained-vector pop and 0x82E7D970 registry-provider selection. The lookup selects a provider by the recorded key from registry 0x8314F2CC. Actual current key, provider result, controller class and lifetime remain unresolved.
replacement.popBranch: With P+0x41 nonzero, 0x82C56638 clears that byte and first requests current virtual +0xE4 on the object from 0x8314F28C at 0x82C56670. A nonempty retained vector supplies its last candidate and the selected local pop adjusts its end. A zero candidate returns locally. For a nonzero candidate, a nonnull sampled current C receives virtual +0 with argument 1 at 0x82C566E4; after normal return P+4 is cleared at 0x82C566E8. The retained candidate is then published to P+4 at 0x82C566EC, its word +8 is copied to P+0x10 and 0x82C56550(P) is requested. This branch has no direct candidate virtual +4 entry request.
replacement.ordinarySelection: With P+0x41 zero, 0x82C56714 requests 0x82E7D970 with P+0x10 and retains its returned candidate. It then requests current virtual +0xE4 on the fresh object from 0x8314F28C at 0x82C56730, before checking candidate zero. Candidate zero returns without local publication; helper effects remain open.
replacement.retainOld: For a nonzero candidate and nonzero P+0x40, the body clears P+0x40 and pushes the currently read P+4 pointer into the retained vector, directly when capacity permits or by requesting 0x821B4450. There is no local nonnull check on the pointer being pushed. Valid vector backing and helper retention are required.
replacement.retireOld: With P+0x40 zero, a nonnull sampled current controller receives virtual +0 with argument 1 at 0x82C567DC, then P+4 is explicitly cleared. The selected vector traversal requests virtual +0 with argument 1 for its nonnull retained elements, walking backward while refreshing the begin pointer after callbacks. Its local end is reset on the completed selected path. These requests do not establish completed destruction or stable vector storage across calls.
replacement.publishBeforeEntry: 0x82C56878 publishes the retained candidate to P+4 before requesting that candidate's current virtual +4 at 0x82C5688C. A nonzero result low byte requests 0x82C56550(P). A zero low byte instead freshly reloads P+4 and requests its current virtual +0x0C at 0x82C568BC without a repeated null guard or a following local P+4 clear. The callback can have changed P+4; no equality with the retained candidate or completed rollback is proved.

deferredReaderReference.requestSites: The retained-vector candidate publication requests 0x82C56550(P) at 0x82C566FC. The ordinary candidate is published before its +4 entry call, whose nonzero result low byte requests 0x82C56550(P) at 0x82C568A0. The queue topic owns reader admission, callback/pop/free ordering, fresh samples and progress qualifications.

retirement.childrenAndQueuedRecords: 0x82C561D8 requests current virtual +0 with argument 1 for each nonnull sampled P+4, P+8 and P+0x2C, clearing each field only after its request returns. For nonnull P+0x0C it instead requests current virtual +0x0C with argument 1 at 0x82C56274 and then clears that field. It then drains the embedded queue by selected metadata updates and conditional queued-record free requests. No direct retained-vector element traversal or outer global-root clear occurs in this body.
retirement.managerStorage: 0x82C56318 installs selected manager table 0x82165680, requests 0x82C561D8, conditionally requests free of retained-vector backing P+0x34 and clears vector begin/end/capacity. It then calls 0x822FDC40(P+0x18). Freeing vector backing is not a direct destructor request for each retained controller.
retirement.embeddedQueueBacking: 0x822FDC40 first decrements its current count to zero without an intervening helper request. Under ordinary retained RAM and no interfering writes this count loop is finite. It then conditionally requests free for each selected block and the backing pointer, and clears container fields +4 and +8. Valid container/backing storage, free-helper return and retention remain prerequisites; whole successful cleanup is not proved.
retirement.outerWrapper: 0x822FDBF0 requests 0x82C56318 and, only after its normal return, conditionally requests 0x82D3D9F0 for the outer object when incoming flag bit 0 is set. Neither this wrapper nor its two selected cleanup bodies directly clears global 0x8314F2E4. The entry boundary owns the separate caller's explicit global clear and later helper-effects qualifications.

compositionPremises: Each read, store and indirect call requires live compatible storage, the actual current target and normal return of preceding requests. Retained candidates, records, vector backing and manager/frame/nonvolatile state must survive relevant callbacks; same-pointer identity is not implied by repeated field names.

Observed local clears occur after selected requests return and apply to the retained manager's current fields. They do not establish completed destruction, completed allocation/free, no reentry or that a callback-published replacement was preserved.

The actual admitted key, selected provider/controller table, queued event generation, key-2/pump invocation route and safe cancellation remain open. Separate H+0x78 loading lifetime, SDK membership, participant retirement, host-wait release and gameplay admission retain their existing gates.
minimalProposal: Any future observer remains default-off, passive and bounded. At existing reads/calls, record numeric update/switch/pop/publish/entry-result/retirement-request categories and opaque manager/controller/vector generations. Keep retained and fresh samples separate, including the entry-zero fresh P+4. A capture declares a finite lifecycle-event cap and dropped-event count; overflow or incomplete pre/post pairs invalidate lifecycle ordering and generation conclusions. Use native-ui-event-queue-boundary.json#/diagnosticBounds for reader observations. Add no getters or behavior changes. Emit no participant identities, payloads, raw pointers, names, credentials, code or full tables.
unrunCases: UNRUN: Actual key-1 update and separate key-2/loading-pump invocation routes, current manager/controller table and supported key categories, including low32 minimum signed input normalization.
UNRUN: Pop empty/nonempty/zero-candidate, provider zero/nonzero, retain-old direct/helper push, retire-old/vector traversal and candidate entry nonzero/zero low-byte paths under valid storage.
UNRUN: Callback-preserved versus callback-replaced current controller, retained candidate/vector generation and the queue topic's reader ownership/finite-progress controls.
UNRUN: Child slot +0 versus +0x0C requests, supported nonempty retained-vector policy and element ownership, backing/free requests, conditional outer free and caller global clear.
UNRUN: Selected lobby class and event record, UI delivery, cancellation/retry, SDK membership/member retirement, host-wait release and gameplay admission remain separate controls.
nextStaticOwners: Select exact key-2 update owner 0x82E60D38 and the framework virtual +8 edge at 0x82D841A4 in the accepted loading loop to determine whether either invokes manager progress. Reuse the accepted APP dispatcher and loading contract. Stop at the first unresolved indirect target or invocation discriminator.

Bind one admitted recorded key to its accepted registry-provider relation, then select that controller's +4/+8/+0x0C/+0 methods needed for entry, key/flag mutation and retirement. Actual controller class during departure C0/C1/C2 remains a generation premise.

Bind the selected P+0x40/P+0x41 writer and retained-vector ownership policy to a supported nonempty-vector path entering 0x82C561D8/0x82C56318. Distinguish current, retained and aliased element owners before interpreting missing direct element-retirement requests or selecting any change.
guards: Local callback/destructor/free requests and subsequent clears do not establish completed destruction, deallocation, rollback or no reentry.
The absence of direct retained-vector element retirement in the selected manager-cleanup bodies does not establish a leak without supported nonempty-vector and ownership premises.
A key-1 update identity or recorded key does not establish a current lobby class or invocation during blocking key-2 entry/loading.
No safe cancellation, completed UI delivery, member retirement, SDK membership, host release or gameplay admission is established.
conclusion: The selected key-1 update requests manager progress, which can update the current controller or select replacement. Replacement publishes an ordinary candidate before its entry request and uses a fresh current-controller request on entry-zero. Cleanup explicitly clears selected children after their requests, while retained-vector element ownership and completed retirement remain unresolved. Deferred UI-reader behavior is owned by the linked queue contract.
